25130300.Description: Predetermined point on the surface of the earth used as a means of controlling movement, a registration Tgt for fire adjustment, or reference for location
25130300.Name: CheckPt

25130500.Description: In land warfare, a point on the terrain, easily identifiable, where two or more units are required to make contact.
25130500.Name: Contact Pt / U (Surface Unknown)

25130600.Description: Designated point at which, in all types of combat, adjacent units/formations must make contact for purposes of control and coordination.
25130600.Name: Coordinating Pt

25130700.Description: A point in space and time, identified during the planning process, where it is anticipated that the commander must make a decision concerning a specific course of action.
25130700.Name: Decision Pt

25131100.Description: A point where two infiltrating elements in the same or different infiltration lanes are scheduled to meet to consolidate before proceeding with their missions.
25131100.Name: Linkup Pt

25131200.Description: A specifically designated place where the passing units will pass through the stationary unit.
25131200.Name: Passage Pt

25131400.Description: An easily identifiable point on the ground at which units can reassemble and reorganize if they become dispersed.
25131400.Name: Rally Pt

25131500.Description: In road movements, a well defined point on a route at which the elements composing a column return under the authority of their respective commanders, each one of these elements continuing its movement towards its own appropriate destination.
25131500.Name: Release Pt

25131600.Description: A well defined point on a route at which a movement of vehicles begins to be under the control of the commander of this movement. It is at this point that the column is formed by the successive passing, at an appointed time, of each of the elements composing the column. In addition to the principal start point of a column there may be secondary start points for its different elements.
25131600.Name: Start Pt

25131800.Description: Designated point or series of points loaded and stored in a global positioning system or other electronic navigational aid system to facilitate movement.
25131800.Name: Waypoint / Destructions of Brs, rds etc

25140603.Name: Friendly Direction of Sp Attk, Dir Arrow

25151403.Description: The principal attack or effort into which the commander throws the full weight of the offensive power at his disposal.
25151403.Name: Main Attk

25151404.Description: An offensive operation carried out in conjunction with a main attack and designed to achieve one or more of the following: a. deceive the enemy; b. destroy or pin down enemy forces which could interfere with the main attack; c. control ground whose occupation by the enemy will hinder the main attack; or d. force the enemy to commit reserves prematurely or in an indecisive area.
25151404.Name: Sp Attk

25160400.Description: A specific place where a unit will cross the line of departure.
25160400.Name: Pt of Departure

25180400.Description: The location at which aircraft quickly gain altitude for Tgt acquisition and engagement.
25180400.Name: Pop-Up Pt (PUP)

25213512.Name: Low Frequency Analyzing and Recording Sonobuoy (LOFAR)

25213515.Name: Vertical Line Array Directional Frequency Analysis and Recording (DIFAR) Sonobuoy

25215400.Name: Mine Warfare Unmanned Underwater Veh Subsurface Sta

25215500.Name: Surface Warfare Unmanned Underwater Veh Subsurface Sta

25216900.Name: Surface Warfare Unmanned Underwater Veh Surface Sta

25218700.Name: Bottom Return/Non-Mine, Mine Like Bottom Object(NOMBO)

25240900.Description: An exact location at sea within a fire support area from which a fire support ship delivers fire.
25240900.Name: Fire Sp Sta

25250400.Description: An exact location at sea within a fire support area from which a fire support ship delivers fire.
25250400.Name: Reload Pt

25270501.Description: An obstacle effect that integrates fire planning and obstacle effort to stop an attacker along a specific avenue of approach or to prevent him from passing through an engagement area.
25270501.Name: Block / Obs Effect

25270502.Description: An obstacle effect that focuses fire planning and obstacle effort to cause the enemy to break up his formation and tempo, interrupt his timetable, commit breaching assets prematurely and attack in a piecemeal effort.
25270502.Name: Disrupt / Obs Effect

25270702.Name: Minefield - Antipersonnel Mine with Directional Effects

25270704.Name: Minefield - Anti Tank Mine with Anti-handling Device

25270705.Name: Minefield - Wide Area Anti Tank Mine

25270707.Name: Minefield - Anti Personnel + Anti Tank Mine

25280200.Description: In land mine warfare, a mine designed to be exploded by the presence, proximity or contact of a person and that will incapacitate,  wound or kill one or more persons.
25280200.Name: Antipersonnel Mine

25280300.Description: A mine designed to immobilize or destroy a tank.
25280300.Name: Anti Tank Mine

25280400.Description: A device intended to protect a mine and which is part of, linked to, attached to or placed under the mine and which activates when an attempt is made to tamper with or otherwise intentionally disturb the mine.
25280400.Name: Anti Tank Mine with Anti-handling Device

25280500.Description: An anti tank mine that detects and acquires Tgts then launches subammunitio n that attacks the top of the Tgts
25280500.Name: Wide Area Anti Tank Mine

25280700.Description: A device designed, constructed or adapted to kill or injure, which functions when a person disturbs or approaches an apparently harmless object or performs an apparently safe act.
25280700.Name: Booby Trap

25280800.Description: Checkpoint to ensure that vehicles do not exceed the capacity of the crossing means and to give drivers final instructions on site-specific procedures and information, such as speed and vehicle interval.
25280800.Name: Engr Regulating Pt

25281903.Name: Tetrahedrons, Dragons Teeth - Movable and Prefabricated

25320100.Description: A location where a patient is transferred from one ambulance to another en route to a medical treatment facility. This may be an established point in an ambulance shuttle system or it may be designated independently.
25320100.Name: Amb Exchange Pt

25320200.Description: An area designated to receive, store, reconfigure and issue Class V material.
25320200.Name: Ammo Sup Pt

25320300.Description: A designated temporary site from which Class V material is transferred to unit vehicles.
25320300.Name: Ammo Transfer Pt

25320500.Description: A specific location where casualties are assembled to be transported to a medical treatment facility, for example, a company aid post.
25320500.Name: Cas Collection Pt

25320600.Description: A specific location where civilians are assembled to be transported to another location.
25320600.Name: Civilian Collection Pt

25320700.Description: A specific location where detainee are assembled to be transported to another location.
25320700.Name: Detainee Collection Pt

25320800.Description: A specific location where enemy prisoners of war are assembled to be transported to another location.
25320800.Name: En Prisoner of War (EPW) Collection Pt

25320900.Description: A specific location where enemy prisoners of war are assembled to be transported to another location.
25320900.Name: Log Release Pt (LRP)

25321000.Description: A point established to collect equipment awaiting repair, controlled exchange, cannibalization, or evacuation. It may be operated by the user or by the direct support maintenance units.
25321000.Name: Maint Collection Pt (MCP)

25321200.Description: A designated point through which a unit passes where it receives fuel, ammunition and other necessary supplies to continue operations.
25321200.Name: Rearm, Refuel and Resupply Pt (R3P)

25321300.Description: An area established to ensure that fuel tanks on combat and fuel servicing vehicles are full before they arrive in the unit’s tactical assembly area
25321300.Name: Refuel On the Move (ROM) Pt

25321400.Description: Manned post used to preclude interruption of traffic flow or movement along designated routes.
25321400.Name: Traffic Con Post (TCP)

25321500.Description: A location where trailers are transferred from one carrier to another while en route.
25321500.Name: Trailer Transfer Pt (TTP)

25321600.Description: A location or series of locations, operated by a battalion maintenance platoon, that is the nearest point to the combat unit to which equipment can be recovered and where limited parts are available and some repairs can be performed.
25321600.Name: Unit Maint Collection Pt (UMCP)

25214803.Name: Fwd Area Arming and Refueling Pt (FAARP)
